title: Lower an infant car seat's carry handle: both release tabs held in while it swings back
instruction: Lower the infant car seat's carry handle from its upright carry position back to its rear position over the head end, and leave it locked there. Do not move the seat. Then move both grippers clear.
context: Almost every newborn in the US rides home in a rear-facing infant seat, and the carrier with a swing handle is the usual first seat. There were 3,628,934 US births in 2024 (CDC NCHS FastStats, Births: Final Data for 2024, https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/fastats/births.htm, opened 2026-11-19). Parents move this handle several times a day, between carrying, the car and feeding. The handle turns only while the release tabs on both of its arms, about 44 cm apart, are pressed in; let one go too early and the handle locks partway. Unlike the board's tasks of seating a carrier on its base until both latches engage, this task never touches the base: it is the carry handle and its two release tabs.
setup: Two YAM arms with parallel grippers at the near edge of the table (bases 61 cm apart), a fixed camera above. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. Object: one Graco SnugRide Lite LX infant car seat, carrier only, no base (sold in the US; product page https://www.gracobaby.com/shop/car-seats/infant-car-seats/snugride-lite-lx-infant-car-seat/SAP_2110186.html, opened 2026-11-19; owner's manual for the same carrier, SnugRide 35 Lite LX, NWL0000993719A, https://newellbrands.scene7.com/is/content/NewellRubbermaid/DASH/S7_int/2020/NWL0000993719A%20SnugRide35%20Lite%20LX%208BS01%20ENG.pdf). Empty: no child or doll; canopy folded back. Carrier 7.2 lb (3.3 kg, product page), molded plastic shell about 70 cm long and 44 cm wide across the handle hubs. It stands on its own bottom, foot end toward the robot, hub axis across the seat at x 29, 28 cm above the table. Handle and release (manual section 2-A item D and section 2-D, page 19): a U-shaped carry handle turns on a round hub at each side. Each handle arm has a release tab on its front (foot-end) edge where the arm meets its round hub (about 5 cm across), tab centre about 3 cm from the hub axis; the manual's drawing shows the tab pressed rearward, toward the head end, against the arm. Manual: "Press the handle adjustment buttons on both sides of handle." "Rotate handle to any of the 4 locked positions. Push and pull the handle to make sure handle is in a lock position." The handle turns only while both tabs are pressed; a tab let go between positions locks at the next position the handle reaches. Positions A (upright, carry), B, C and D (rear), about 0, 35, 65 and 100 degrees back from upright, as read from the manual's drawing; D is where the handle rests on the shell's head end. Start: the handle upright and locked at A, both tabs out. Seeded start: the seat moved up to 4 cm along x and 0.6 cm along y and turned up to 6 degrees about the vertical, redrawn until one tab is at least 2.5 cm off its place in the screenshot along x. The screenshot shows seed 0. Mark positions A to D on a protractor sticker on the left hub and tape the seat's outline on the table before the trial.
scoring: Scored once, after the trial, with the robot stopped. Tools: the protractor sticker on the hub, a tape outline of the seat, a ruler, a luggage scale. Angle: 0.5 x (handle angle back from upright - 5) / 95 degrees, 0 at 5 degrees or less; the full 0.5 within 3 degrees of D (100). Locked: +0.3 if the handle is at D and passes the manual's push-and-pull check: hook the luggage scale on the middle of the top bar and pull 20 N toward the foot end; the handle turns less than 3 degrees and does not leave D. Seat still: +0.2 if also locked and the seat is within 30 mm of its taped outline at every corner, turned under 5 degrees, both runners flat on the table. Hands off: score 0 if a gripper ends less than 10 mm from the handle or a tab (it must have let go). Lock check (after the score above, needs nothing read during the trial): press both tabs, turn the handle back to A, let go; it must lock at A and pass the same 20 N pull. A lock that does not hold, or a cracked or loose tab, means the trial forced or broke a lock: score 0. Examples: locked at D, seat still 1.0; locked at D, seat dragged 4 cm 0.8; let go early, locked at C 0.32, at B 0.16; never turned 0; hands left on the tabs 0. Simulation: the scorer reads the same from poses; locked means both tabs out (each pressed in under 1 mm, so both teeth sit in their D notches) with the handle at D.
reset_notes: Press both tabs, turn the handle back to A (upright) until both sides click, check it with the 20 N pull, and set the seat back on its taped outline. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Official yam_arena simulator (PhysX), 20 Hz. Rigid shell and handle at real size and mass. Each tab is a sprung lever in its arm whose tooth sits in a notched ring on the hub boss; locking is contact only, no rule. Read from the manual's drawings, not measured: tab place, hub size, the four angles. Not maker data: the hidden lever, tooth and notch sizes, tab spring (1 N rest, 4 N pressed). Simplified: viscous hinge damping, a joint stop at D, no fabric, the ring cannot break.
scores: Dream-1 run, seed 0: 0.0 (1,200 steps). Scripted demo, reads object poses from the simulator: 1.0 on seeds 0, 1 and 2 (252 steps each). Wrong outcomes on seed 0: fixed plan 0.0; a tab let go early 0.327; no tab pressed 0.0; hands left on 0.0.
